doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Jelly Roll Morton as a boy on the Gulf Coast
summary: Billy says Morton lived with them in Bay St. Louis and traveled around Mississippi; as a kid he already played tunes he later recorded, such as The Pearls.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Oh, can you tell me a little bit more about Jolly Roll Martin before we quit? I don't want to take your whole afternoon, but if you can, uh, when he comes to the New Orleans, uh, when he traveled with you, you say he came from, uh, around Bay St. Louis. Yeah.
Well, he didn't come up here with us, but he'd go into New Orleans, and up and down the coast, Scranton, and, well, obviously. And then he lived with us, you know.
We had always kept house, you see, and then, for fun, we just lived there, you know.
And his grandmother, we always lived with her when we'd go to Bay St. Louis, the room, you know, she'd do this room. And we got to, uh, that's how we got to know Jolly Roll.

And, uh, he went around in Mississippi and, and, you know, Spartan, Louisiana with us from time to time. And he was a fine kid, and he always did the things that he recorded later when he got to be a young man. He played all that stuff when he was a kid. stuff like stuff like
the pearls and the jelly roll blues and the whining boy.
Yeah, the jelly roll blues. King Porter, did he know?
He hesitated, must have hesitated. And I used to use that in the show, you remember?
